researched_by: user report from a visit (Fontburn), plus operator pages and user forums for the rest
policy_summary:
A company-wide scheme, not a site arrangement. Overnight parking is permitted and charged at reservoirs across the north east, with a shared booking system covering Balderhead, Derwent, Fontburn, Selset, Grassholme, Scaling Dam and Kielder. Typically GBP10 a night with no facilities - no hook-up, no waste disposal - and rangers check tickets in the evening.

This is the answer to whether water companies are a per-site or per-company research job. Per company. One operator, one scheme, seven reservoirs. If United Utilities and Yorkshire Water work the same way, the landowner tier is far smaller work than the councils.
notes: Kielder is the exception and needs care - see the Kielder note below. Elsewhere the pattern looks consistent: pay at the visitor centre or online, ranger checks in the evening, gates close overnight.
open_questions: Confirm the current price at each reservoir - GBP10 is reported at Fontburn and Derwent.
Which reservoirs have gates that lock, and at what time? Derwent reported as closing with reopening at 08:00.
Do other water companies run equivalent schemes? That decides the size of the whole landowner tier.

sites.search_hint: Tower Knowe Visitor Centre, Kielder Water
sites.notes: Approved for overnight stays. GBP10 a night and unusually it accepts caravans as well as motorhomes and campervans - most sites do not. No electric hook-up, no waste disposal. Pre-pay at bookwhen.com/car-parking. Visitor centre and cafe on site.

sites.name: Hawkhope, South Abutment, Matthew's Linn, Bakethin and Skyspace Lower
sites.notes: NOT approved for overnight stays, whatever the day ticket implies. This is where visitor reports went wrong: the GBP6.50 day ticket runs until 03:00 for stargazing and is transferable across every car park, so it reads as though it covers the night. It does not. Rangers patrol and CCTV covers the car parks. One party paid the day fee plus GBP10 at Hawkhope and were still moved on at 21:00.

sites.name: Kielder day parking (all car parks)
sites.price_note: GBP6.50 full day until 03:00, GBP2.50 for one hour. Transferable across every Kielder car park.
sites.notes: Included because the day ticket is the single most misleading thing at Kielder. It lasts until 3am for stargazing and works in every car park, which reads like permission to stay the night. It is not. Only four car parks are approved for overnight: Tower Knowe, Kielder Castle, Elf Kirk and the Anglers Arms rear car park.

kielder_note:
RESOLVED. Kielder Waterside is owned and operated by Northumbrian Water. The wider park is run by the Kielder Water & Forest Park Development Trust, whose members include Northumbrian Water, the Forestry Commission, Northumberland County Council, Calvert Trust Kielder and Kielder Observatory.

The contradiction in visitor reports is explained. Overnight stays are approved at FOUR places only: Tower Knowe (Northumbrian Water, GBP10), Kielder Castle (Forestry England, GBP15), Elf Kirk viewpoint, and the Anglers Arms rear car park in Kielder village. Hawkhope is NOT one of them.

The trap is the day ticket. GBP6.50 buys a full day until 03:00 for stargazing and is transferable across every car park in the park - Hawkhope, South Abutment, Tower Knowe, Kielder Waterside, Matthew's Linn, Bakethin, Kielder Castle, Skyspace Lower and Elf Kirk. Being transferable, and running until 3am, it reads like it covers staying the night. It does not. The party who paid GBP5 for the day and GBP10 for the night at Hawkhope had bought something that does not apply there, and were moved on at 21:00. Correctly, as it turns out.
